record.context_brief: Maximal distance in sets of lengths
record.original_question: Let G = C_{n1} ⊕ ··· ⊕ C_{nr} be a finite abelian group with |G| >= 3 and 1 < n1 | ··· | nr. For a set of lengths A, let Delta(A) be the set of positive integers that occur as gaps between consecutive elements of A, and let Delta(G) be the union of these distance sets over all sets of lengths arising from G. Is the largest possible distance equal to max{nr - 2, -1 + sum_{i=1}^r floor(ni/2)}?

evidence.quote: Let A subset Z. Then the set of distances of A, denoted by Delta(A), is the set of all differences between consecutive elements of A. For an atomic monoid H, we denote by Delta(H) the set of distances of H.
However, in general the following problem is wide open. Problem 5.7. Let G ~= C_{n1} ⊕ ··· ⊕ C_{nr} with |G| >= 3 and 1 < n1 | ··· | nr. Is max Delta(G) = max{nr - 2, -1 + sum floor(ni/2)}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite abelian group with |G| ≥ 3, written in invariant form as G ≅ C_{n_1} ⊕ C_{n_2} ⊕ ··· ⊕ C_{n_r} with 1 < n_1 | n_2 | ··· | n_r. Let B(G) denote the monoid of zero-sum sequences over G (the monoid of all finite sequences of elements of G, with concatenation, whose elements sum to 0), whose atoms are the minimal zero-sum sequences. For an element S ∈ B(G), let L(S) ⊆ ℤ_{≥0} denote the set of lengths of S, i.e. the set of all integers k such that S admits a factorization S = U_1 · U_2 · ··· · U_k into atoms. For a finite subset A ⊂ ℤ with |A| ≥ 2, written A = {a_0 < a_1 < ··· < a_k}, define the set of distances 
Δ(A) = { a_i − a_{i−1} : 1 ≤ i ≤ k }.
Define
Δ(G) = ⋃_{S ∈ B(G), |L(S)| ≥ 2} Δ(L(S)).

Determine whether 
max Δ(G) = max{ n_r − 2,  −1 + ∑_{i=1}^{r} ⌊ n_i / 2 ⌋ }.
artifact.category_tag: Sets of lengths in Krull monoids
artifact.status_search_result: The exact value of max Δ(G) for general finite abelian groups remains a standing open problem. It is known for cyclic groups (max Δ(C_n) = n − 2) and for some special classes, with the conjectured formula max{n_r − 2, −1 + Σ⌊n_i/2⌋} being the working hypothesis. Recent surveys and papers on Krull monoids and sets of lengths continue to list the precise determination of max Δ(G) as unresolved in general.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Class Groups of Krull Monoids Via Their Systems of Sets of Lengths: A Status Report
status_evidence.snippet: For Krull monoids with finite class group G, the set of distances Δ(H) depends only on G; precise determination of invariants such as max Δ(G) in general remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Determining max Δ(G) for general finite abelian groups is an open problem in the theory of sets of lengths.

status_evidence.title: On Delta Sets and their Realizable Subsets in Krull Monoids with Cyclic Class Groups
status_evidence.snippet: For cyclic class groups of order n ≥ 3 one has Δ(G) ⊆ {1,...,n−2} and equality holds, but the structure for higher rank is only partially understood.
status_evidence.claim: The cyclic case is settled with max Δ(C_n) = n − 2; higher rank cases remain conjectural.
